name: Gainium
description: Create, run, and analyze crypto trading bots

authentication.name: Provider-native Gainium API key
authentication.description: Connect Gainium with an API key and API secret.
authentication.notes: Gainium V2 requires both an API key and an API secret. MindCloud stores the API secret so requests can be signed with HMAC-SHA256; the secret itself is not sent as a plain request header.

credentials.name: API Secret
credentials.description: Used to sign Gainium API requests with HMAC-SHA256.

setupGuide.title: Set up Gainium API credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Gainium requires two-factor authentication before you can create API keys.

steps.title: Create a new API access token
steps.description: In Gainium, click "New API access token." Give the token a descriptive name so you can recognize it later.

steps.title: Choose the token settings
steps.description: Select the permission scope you want, choose the trading mode, and optionally restrict the token to a specific bot ID before you click Create.

steps.title: Copy the API key and API secret
steps.description: Copy both values immediately and store them securely. MindCloud needs the API key and the API secret to authenticate and sign requests.

setupGuide.title: Get your gBizINFO API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the gBizINFO Web API application form and the email account that will receive the token.

steps.description: Enter the requested contact details, your intended API use, and submit the form using the email address where you want to receive the token.

steps.title: Copy the issued API token
steps.description: Wait for gBizINFO to send the token to your registered email address, then copy the token value exactly as issued.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud

name: Geocodio

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Geocodio API key for authenticated API requests.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Use an existing API key or create a separate key for MindCloud so access can be revoked independently later.

steps.title: Review endpoint permissions
steps.description: By default, Geocodio API keys can access single and batch geocoding. Enable Lists API or Distance API permissions in the Geocodio dashboard before using list or distance actions.

name: GitHub

setupGuide.title: Create a GitHub OAuth app
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the GitHub account that will own the OAuth app. Have the MindCloud callback URL ready before you register the app.

steps.title: Open GitHub Developer settings
steps.description: In GitHub, open Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth apps.

steps.title: Create a new OAuth app
steps.description: Click OAuth apps, then click New OAuth App. If you have never created one before, the button is Register a new application.

steps.title: Enter the public app details
steps.description: Set Application name and Homepage URL. Application description is optional and visible to users.

steps.title: Set the authorization callback URL
steps.description: Paste the MindCloud callback URL into Authorization callback URL. GitHub OAuth apps support only one callback URL.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.description: Click Register application to create the OAuth app.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud auth settings
steps.description: Use the GitHub OAuth app's Client ID and Client Secret in the MindCloud authentication settings to complete the connection.

description: GitHub Utils provides utility actions for repositories, issues, pull requests, commits, files, releases, and workflow runs through the GitHub REST API.

authentication.name: GitHub OAuth
authentication.description: Connect with GitHub OAuth to access repository and workflow utility actions.
authentication.notes: GitHub OAuth web application flow uses /login/oauth/authorize and exchanges the authorization code at /login/oauth/access_token. Use Bearer tokens for GitHub REST API requests. The selected scopes support private repository utilities, user profile/email lookup, and workflow actions.

setupGuide.title: Create a GitHub OAuth app
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the GitHub account that will own the OAuth app. Have the MindCloud callback URL ready before you register the app.

steps.title: Open GitHub Developer settings
steps.description: In GitHub, open Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth apps.

steps.title: Create a new OAuth app
steps.description: Click OAuth apps, then click New OAuth App. If this is your first OAuth app, GitHub may label the button Register a new application.

steps.title: Enter the public app details
steps.description: Set Application name and Homepage URL. Application description is optional and visible to users.

steps.title: Set the authorization callback URL
steps.description: Paste the MindCloud callback URL into Authorization callback URL. GitHub OAuth apps support one callback URL.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.description: Click Register application to create the OAuth app.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud auth settings
steps.description: Use the GitHub OAuth app Client ID and Client Secret in the MindCloud authentication settings to complete the connection.

steps.title: Create a bearer token with POST /auth/login

steps.title: Paste the bearer token into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the returned access_token as the GitScrum connection secret. When the token expires, generate a fresh token or refresh it with POST /auth/refresh and reconnect.

arguments.name: Creation Date To
arguments.description: Restricts the list of returned orders to the ones created before (or on) the provided datetime. This parameter should use the following format yyyy-mm-ddThh:MM (year, month, day, 24-hour and minute) and be expressed in UTC time.

arguments.name: Delivery Date From
arguments.description: Restricts the list of returned orders to the ones whose selected delivery slot lands after (or on) the provided datetime. This parameter should use the following format yyyy-mm-ddThh:MM (year, month, day, 24-hour and minute) and be expressed in UTC time. When this filter is applied, orders that do not have a selected delivery slot (shipped by transporter, for instance) will not be returned. Also, note that a delivery slot is said to land after a given datetime if its slot_start value is later than that datetime.

arguments.name: Delivery Date To

When this filter is applied, orders that do not have a selected delivery slot (shipped by transporter, for instance) will not be returned. Also, note that a delivery slot is said to land before a given datetime if its slot_end value comes before that datetime.

actions.name: Create Order Batch
actions.description: Creates a new order batch in Goody.

arguments.name: From Name
arguments.description: The name of the sender of the order (typically a gift), to be displayed as "from".

arguments.name: Message
arguments.description: For gifts, a message for the gift to be displayed in the digital unwrapping and email notifications, if enabled.

arguments.name: Send Method
arguments.description: The method for sending a order batch. `email_and_link` sends a gift email to the recipient (specify `email` for each recipient). `link_multiple_custom_list` generates a gift link without an automatic email. `direct_send` ships the product directly to the recipient (specify `mailing_address` for each recipient). For more information, see [Send Methods](/introduction/send-methods).

arguments.name: Card ID
arguments.description: The digital greeting card to attach to gifts. A card must be specified if a message is specified, since the message is displayed after the card is opened.

arguments.name: Payment Method ID
arguments.description: The payment method used to pay for this order batch. If not specified, defaults to the first payment method on the account. If the account has no payment methods, then the order batch creation will fail.

arguments.name: Workspace ID
arguments.description: Workspace to create the order batch in. If not specified, creates the order batch in the oldest workspace the user has access to.

arguments.name: Scheduled Send On
arguments.description: The date and time at which the order batch will be sent. If not specified, the order batch is sent immediately. If an order batch is scheduled to be sent in the future, then orders will not be created until the scheduled send time. ISO 8601 format.

arguments.name: Expires At
arguments.description: The date and time at which the order batch will expire. If not specified, the order batch does not expire. An expiry must be set for orders paid using account balance. ISO 8601 format.

arguments.name: Swap
arguments.description: What method to use to allow recipients to swap their gift. `single` (default) allows the recipient to swap the gift for one item, with hidden gift prices. `multiple` allows them to swap for multiple items up to the gift cost, with gift prices shown. `disabled` disables swapping on the gift. For gift collections (gift of choice), this must not be `disabled`.

arguments.name: International Shipping Tier
arguments.description: Whether to enable international shipping on this order. `disabled` (default) only enables US shipping on this order. `standard` combined with `international_gift_cards_enabled` enables international gift cards. `full` enables the full global catalog for 100+ countries, with additional tax, duties, and freight costs.

arguments.name: International Gift Cards Enabled
arguments.description: Whether to enable international gift cards on this order. If `true` and the `international_shipping_tier` is `standard`, then international gift cards can be swapped to. If `false`, then international gift cards are not available to be swapped to.

arguments.name: Notifications Enabled
arguments.description: Direct Send only. Whether to enable notifications for Direct Send orders. If `true`, we send confirmation and shipping notifications to Direct Send recipients. If `false`, we do not send any notifications to Direct Send recipients.

name: Google Cloud Document AI
description: Use Google Cloud Document AI to extract, classify, train, evaluate, and manage document processors through the stable v1 REST API.

authentication.name: Google OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect with Google OAuth 2.0 using the cloud-platform scope for Google Cloud Document AI.
authentication.notes: Connect with a Google account that has IAM permissions for the target Google Cloud project and Document AI resources. Runtime action calls also need the Document AI API enabled in that project.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Cloud Document AI
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Google Cloud project where the Document AI API is enabled. Your Google account needs IAM permissions for the Document AI resources you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open Document AI in Google Cloud
steps.description: Sign in with the Google account you want to connect and open Document AI.

steps.title: Select the Google Cloud project
steps.description: Use the project picker at the top of Google Cloud and select the project that contains the processors and schemas you want to use.

steps.title: Confirm the location
steps.description: Use the processor list or processor details page to confirm the Document AI location, such as us or eu. MindCloud actions ask for this value as Location ID.

steps.title: Connect with Google
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, start the Google OAuth connection, and approve the cloud-platform scope.

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate Google Cloud Document AI with a Google Cloud service account private key.
authentication.notes: Uses Google service-account server-to-server OAuth. MindCloud signs a short-lived JWT with the service account private key, exchanges it for a Google OAuth access token, and sends that token as a Document AI bearer token. Grant the service account only the IAM roles needed for the intended processors, processor versions, and schemas. Batch operations can also require access to any Google Cloud Storage locations referenced by the workflow.

credentials.name: Project ID
credentials.description: The Google Cloud project ID that contains the Document AI resources this connection should access.

credentials.name: Client Email
credentials.description: The client_email value from the service account key JSON file.

credentials.name: Private Key ID
credentials.description: Optional legacy field from the service account key JSON file. The Google auth SDK can mint Document AI access tokens with only project ID, client email, and private key.

credentials.name: Private Key
credentials.description: The private_key value from the service account key JSON file. MindCloud uses it only to sign short-lived Google OAuth JWT assertions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Cloud Document AI with a service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need permission in Google Cloud to create or access a service account key, the Document AI API must be enabled in the selected project, and the service account must already have IAM access to the processors, schemas, and any related Cloud Storage resources your workflows will use.

steps.title: Open the Service accounts page
steps.description: Open the Google Cloud Service accounts page and select the Google Cloud project that contains the Document AI processors this connection should access.

steps.title: Create or choose a service account
steps.description: Create a service account for MindCloud, or open an existing service account that should be used for this connection.

steps.title: Grant Document AI access
steps.description: Grant the service account the smallest IAM roles that support the actions you plan to run. At minimum, it needs access to the target Document AI processors and schemas. If your workflows use batch processing with Cloud Storage input or output, also grant the required Cloud Storage IAM roles on those buckets.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the Keys tab for the service account, choose Add key, create a new JSON key, and download the key file.

steps.title: Copy the required values into MindCloud
steps.description: Open the downloaded JSON file and copy project_id into Project ID, client_email into Client Email, private_key_id into Private Key ID, and private_key into Private Key.

name: Google Cloud Pub/Sub
description: Publish, subscribe, and manage Pub/Sub topics, subscriptions, and schemas

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Authorize Google Cloud Pub/Sub with a Google OAuth 2.0 web application.
authentication.notes: Google OAuth apps in Testing only work for listed test users. Pub/Sub methods request Google scopes and may require Google verification before broader production rollout.

setupGuide.title: Connect a Google OAuth 2.0 web app
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Google Cloud project with the Pub/Sub API enabled and permission to configure Google Auth Platform.

steps.title: Configure the consent screen
steps.description: In Google Auth Platform, set the app name, support email, homepage, authorized domains, requested Pub/Sub scopes, and any test users you need while the app is in Testing.

steps.title: Create a Web application client
steps.description: Open Google Auth Platform Clients, create a client, choose Web application, and register the exact authorized redirect URI that MindCloud expects for this app before saving.

steps.title: Save the client ID and client secret in MindCloud
steps.description: Replace the placeholder client ID and client secret in this authentication with the real values from Google. Google only shows the client secret when the client is created.

steps.title: Authorize with a test user first
steps.description: If the Google app is still in Testing, sign in with a Google account that you added as a test user before broader rollout.

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate Google Cloud Pub/Sub with a Google Cloud service account private key.
authentication.notes: Uses Google service-account server-to-server OAuth. MindCloud signs a short-lived JWT with the service account private key, exchanges it for a Google OAuth access token, and sends that token as a Pub/Sub bearer token. Grant the service account only the IAM roles needed for the intended topics, subscriptions, schemas, and message operations.

credentials.name: Project ID
credentials.description: The Google Cloud project ID that contains the Pub/Sub resources this connection should access.

credentials.name: Client Email
credentials.description: The client_email value from the service account key JSON file.

credentials.name: Private Key ID
credentials.description: Optional legacy field from the service account key JSON file. The Google auth SDK can mint Pub/Sub access tokens with only project ID, client email, and private key.

credentials.name: Private Key
credentials.description: The private_key value from the service account key JSON file. MindCloud uses it only to sign short-lived Google OAuth JWT assertions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Cloud Pub/Sub with a service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need permission in Google Cloud to create or access a service account key, the Pub/Sub API must be enabled in the selected project, and the service account must already have IAM access to the topics, subscriptions, or schemas your workflows will use.

steps.title: Open the Service accounts page
steps.description: Open the Google Cloud Service accounts page and select the Google Cloud project that contains the Pub/Sub resources this connection should access.

steps.title: Create or choose a service account
steps.description: Create a service account for MindCloud, or open an existing service account that should be used for this connection.

steps.title: Grant Pub/Sub access
steps.description: Grant the service account the smallest Pub/Sub IAM roles that support the actions you plan to run, such as Publisher, Subscriber, Viewer, or Editor on the required topics, subscriptions, and schemas.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the Keys tab for the service account, choose Add key, create a new JSON key, and download the key file.

steps.title: Copy the required values into MindCloud
steps.description: Open the downloaded JSON file and copy project_id into Project ID, client_email into Client Email, private_key_id into Private Key ID, and private_key into Private Key.

credentials.name: Project ID
credentials.description: The Google Cloud Project ID that contains the Cloud Storage bucket you want to use. You can find it in Google Cloud Console from the project selector at the top of the page.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Cloud Storage
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Google Cloud project that contains the buckets you want to use. The connection form asks for the Google Cloud Project ID, not the project name or project number. If your organization enforces Google Cloud session control and you see a reauthentication error, a Google Workspace admin may need to trust the OAuth app before you reconnect.

steps.title: Open the Google Cloud Welcome page
steps.description: Sign in with the Google account you want to use for this storage connection.

steps.title: Select the correct project
steps.description: Use the project picker at the top of the page and select the project that owns the Cloud Storage buckets this connection should access.

steps.title: Copy the Project ID
steps.description: On the Welcome page, copy the Project ID value. Do not use the project name or project number.

steps.title: Enter the Project ID
steps.description: Return to the connection form, paste the copied value into the Project ID field, and continue the OAuth connection flow.

steps.title: If Google requires reauthentication, open API controls
steps.description: Ask a Google Workspace admin to go to admin.google.com, then open Security > Access and data control > API controls.

steps.title: Find the OAuth app
steps.description: Click Manage App Access. Check Accessed apps if the user already connected the app, or go to Configured apps and add an app by OAuth app name or client ID. Paste this OAuth client ID: 75190365279-09qj5dhb7uoc33pgrf8s1rkjrt4grqgl.apps.googleusercontent.com.

steps.title: Set access to Trusted
steps.description: Select the OAuth app or client IDs, open Access to Google data, choose Trusted for the relevant organizational unit, and save the change.

steps.title: Exempt trusted apps from Google Cloud session control
steps.description: In the Google Admin console, open Security > Access and data control > Google Cloud session control, select the relevant organizational unit, and check Exempt trusted apps.

steps.title: Reconnect the account
steps.description: After the admin saves the settings, reconnect the Google Cloud Storage account from the connection form and rerun the workflow.

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate Google Cloud Storage with a Google Cloud service account private key.
authentication.notes: Uses Google service-account server-to-server OAuth. MindCloud signs a short-lived JWT with the service account private key, exchanges it for a Google OAuth access token, and sends that token as a Cloud Storage bearer token. Grant the service account only the IAM roles needed for the intended bucket/object operations.

credentials.name: Project ID
credentials.description: The Google Cloud project ID that contains the Cloud Storage buckets this connection should access.

credentials.name: Client Email
credentials.description: The client_email value from the service account key JSON file.

credentials.name: Private Key
credentials.description: The private_key value from the service account key JSON file. MindCloud uses it only to sign short-lived Google OAuth JWT assertions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Cloud Storage with a service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need permission in Google Cloud to create a service account key or access an existing key, and the service account must have IAM access to the buckets or objects you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open the Service accounts page
steps.description: Open the Google Cloud Service accounts page and select the Google Cloud project that contains the storage resources for this connection.

steps.title: Create or choose a service account
steps.description: Create a service account for MindCloud, or open an existing service account that should be used for this connection.

steps.title: Grant Cloud Storage access
steps.description: Grant the service account the smallest Cloud Storage IAM role that supports the actions you plan to run. For object-only read and write operations, use Storage Object Admin. For bucket creation or bucket updates, use Storage Admin or a custom role with the required bucket permissions.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the Keys tab for the service account, choose Add key, create a new JSON key, and download the key file.

steps.title: Copy the required values into MindCloud
steps.description: Open the downloaded JSON file and copy project_id into Project ID, client_email into Client Email, private_key_id into Private Key ID, and private_key into Private Key.

name: Google Dialogflow
description: Build and manage Google Dialogflow CX conversational agents, flows, intents, entity types, pages, and webhooks through the Dialogflow API.

authentication.name: Google OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect with a Google account that has access to Dialogflow CX resources.
authentication.notes: Uses Google OAuth 2.0 for web server applications. Request the Dialogflow scope for least-privilege access.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Dialogflow
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a Google account that can access the Google Cloud project containing your Dialogflow CX resources. The Dialogflow API must be enabled for that project.

steps.title: Confirm project access
steps.description: In Google Cloud, confirm that your account has permission to view and manage the Dialogflow CX project and location you plan to use.

steps.title: Connect with Google
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, start the Google Dialogflow connection, choose the Google account with project access, and approve the requested Dialogflow permission.

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate Google Dialogflow with a Google Cloud service account private key.
authentication.notes: Uses Google service-account server-to-server OAuth. MindCloud signs a short-lived JWT with the service account private key, exchanges it for a Google OAuth access token, and sends that token as a Dialogflow bearer token. Grant the service account only the IAM roles needed for the intended agents, flows, pages, intents, entity types, and webhooks.

credentials.name: Project ID
credentials.description: The Google Cloud project ID that contains the Dialogflow resources this connection should access.

credentials.name: Client Email
credentials.description: The client_email value from the service account key JSON file.

credentials.name: Private Key ID
credentials.description: Optional legacy field from the service account key JSON file. The Google auth SDK can mint Dialogflow access tokens with only project ID, client email, and private key.

credentials.name: Private Key
credentials.description: The private_key value from the service account key JSON file. MindCloud uses it only to sign short-lived Google OAuth JWT assertions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Dialogflow with a service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need permission in Google Cloud to create or access a service account key, the Dialogflow API must be enabled in the selected project, and the service account must already have IAM access to the Dialogflow agents and related resources your workflows will use.

steps.title: Open the Service accounts page
steps.description: Open the Google Cloud Service accounts page and select the Google Cloud project that contains the Dialogflow resources this connection should access.

steps.title: Create or choose a service account
steps.description: Create a service account for MindCloud, or open an existing service account that should be used for this connection.

steps.title: Grant Dialogflow access
steps.description: Grant the service account the smallest Dialogflow and Google Cloud IAM roles that support the actions you plan to run for the target agents and locations.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the Keys tab for the service account, choose Add key, create a new JSON key, and download the key file.

steps.title: Copy the required values into MindCloud
steps.description: Open the downloaded JSON file and copy project_id into Project ID, client_email into Client Email, private_key_id into Private Key ID, and private_key into Private Key.

actions.name: Validate Address
actions.description: Validates an Address

arguments.name: Region Code
arguments.description: Optional, but helpful for a complete validation. i.e. `CA` for Canada.

arguments.name: Address Lines
arguments.description:
Required. Unstructured address lines describing the lower levels of an address.

Because values in addressLines do not have type information and may sometimes contain multiple values in a single field (e.g. "Austin, TX"), it is important that the line order is clear. The order of address lines should be "envelope order" for the country/region of the address.

The minimum permitted structural representation of an address consists of all information placed in the addressLines. If a regionCode is not provided, the region is inferred from the address lines.

Creating an address only containing addressLines, and then geocoding is the recommended way to handle completely unstructured addresses (as opposed to guessing which parts of the address should be localities or administrative areas).

name: Google Slides
description: Create presentations, collaborate on slides, present live, and share recordings.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Slides
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Google Cloud project where you can enable APIs, configure the Google Auth platform, and create OAuth client credentials for a web application.

steps.title: Open Google Cloud Console
steps.description: Sign in to Google Cloud Console with the account that owns the Google Slides integration project.

steps.title: Select or create the Google Cloud project
steps.description: Use the project that will own the Google Slides API and OAuth client for this MindCloud connector.

steps.title: Enable the Google Slides API
steps.description: Enable the Google Slides API in the selected project before creating OAuth credentials.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen in Google Auth platform
steps.description: In Google Cloud Console, go to Google Auth platform > Branding and complete the app information, support email, audience, and contact information flow. If Google Auth platform is not configured yet, click Get Started and finish the setup flow.

steps.title: Add test users if the app is External and still in Testing
steps.description: If you selected External for the audience and the app is not yet published, go to Google Auth platform > Audience and add the operator email address as a test user before attempting the connection.

steps.title: Add the connector scopes in Data Access when required
steps.description: If this app is used outside of your organization, go to Google Auth platform > Data Access and add the scopes requested by this connector so the consent screen matches the requested access.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.description: Go to Google Auth platform > Clients, click Create Client, choose Application type > Web application, and create a client for the MindCloud Google Slides connector.

steps.title: Add the authorized redirect URI
steps.description: Under the Web application client, add this authorized redirect URI exactly: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/googleSlides/callback

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the generated client ID and client secret when creating the MindCloud connection, then complete the Google consent flow in MindCloud.

name: Google Workspace Admin
description: Google Workspace Admin SDK scaffold for user directory automation.

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate Google Workspace Admin with a Google Cloud service account using Domain-Wide Delegation.
authentication.notes: This connection only works when a Google Workspace super admin has explicitly authorized Domain-Wide Delegation for the service account client ID in the Google Admin console. A normal Google login is not enough. If the service account is not authorized, or if the impersonated admin user does not have sufficient admin privileges, MindCloud requests will fail with errors such as 'Not Authorized to access this resource/api' or 'insufficient permissions'. WARNING: Use the smallest set of admin scopes possible and only connect this app for trusted internal administration workflows.

credentials.name: Service Account Client ID
credentials.description: Required for Domain-Wide Delegation. Enter the numeric client_id from the service account JSON. A Google Workspace super admin must authorize this exact client ID in Admin console > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation before this connection can work.

credentials.name: Client Email
credentials.description: Enter the client_email value from the service account JSON key. This is the service account identity that MindCloud uses to request delegated access.

credentials.name: Private Key ID
credentials.description: Enter the private_key_id value from the service account JSON key. This helps identify which service account key is being used.

credentials.name: Private Key
credentials.description: Enter the private_key value from the service account JSON key exactly as provided, including the BEGIN and END PRIVATE KEY lines. Keep this value secret.

credentials.name: Delegated Admin Email
credentials.description: Enter the email address of the Google Workspace admin user that MindCloud should impersonate. This must be a super admin or a delegated admin that already has the required user, group, and organizational unit privileges.

setupGuide.title: Connect Google Workspace Admin with Domain-Wide Delegation
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Google Workspace super admin, a Google Cloud project, the Admin SDK API enabled, a service account with Domain-Wide Delegation enabled, and a secure way to store the downloaded JSON key. MindCloud will impersonate the admin email you provide when calling the Directory API.

steps.title: Create or choose a service account
steps.description: Open the Google Cloud project that will own this integration, then create a new service account for MindCloud or choose an existing one.

steps.title: Enable Domain-Wide Delegation on the service account
steps.description: Open the service account details and enable Google Workspace Domain-Wide Delegation. Copy the numeric OAuth Client ID shown for the service account. You will need that value in the Admin console and in MindCloud.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the Keys tab for the service account, create a new JSON key, and download the key file securely. You will copy values from this file into MindCloud.

steps.title: Authorize the service account in Google Admin console
steps.description: Sign in as a Google Workspace super admin. Open Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation, add the service account OAuth Client ID, and authorize exactly these scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.orgunit.

steps.title: Choose the impersonated admin user carefully
steps.description: Decide which admin email MindCloud should impersonate. This should be a super admin or a delegated admin that already has the user, group, and organizational unit privileges your workflows require.

steps.title: Copy the required values into MindCloud

Enter your OData Service Document URL.
Example:
`https://eval.grandavenue.com/MindCloud/odata/v2` 

To find yours, follow these steps:
1. Navigate to `Administrative Actions > Configure System > Configure Connector > Configure OData API`
2. Under `OData API Versions` right click and copy the `OData Service Document URL`.
3. Past the full URL here.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Grist account or organization that owns the docs you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open your Grist profile settings
steps.description: In Grist, open the account menu in the top-right corner and select Profile Settings.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.description: In the API section, click Create to generate a new API key for your account.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the new API key and store it somewhere secure because you will use it in MindCloud.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the copied value into the API Key field for this Grist connection.

setupGuide.title: Connect Guru with a token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need either a Guru user token or a Guru collection token.

steps.title: Open Guru API token settings
steps.description: In Guru, go to Admin -> API Tokens.

steps.title: Create the token you want to use
steps.description: Create a User Token for read/write access, or create a Collection Token for read-only access to one collection.

steps.title: Copy the required values
steps.description: For a User Token, copy your Guru account email and the token. For a Collection Token, copy the collection ID and the token.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Use Basic auth. For a User Token, set Username to your Guru email and Password to the token. For a Collection Token, set Username to the collection ID and Password to the token.

name: gyfti
description: Use gyfti to automate gift campaigns, store users, wallet pool updates, and webhook registrations for campaign and store events.

authentication.name: Bearer Token
authentication.description: Use a gyfti access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Connect gyfti
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a valid gyfti access token. gyfti documents generating one by calling the login endpoint with the account email and password.

steps.title: Generate an access token
steps.description: Follow gyfti's authentication documentation to call the login endpoint and get the response token for your account.

steps.title: Paste the token
steps.description: Paste the returned token into the API Key field in the connection form.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.description: Run the connection test. A valid token returns the logged-in user state from gyfti.
